1.b3 e5 2.a3 d5 3.c3.strategy: Builds a pawn wall but blocks its own bishop: with pawns on b3 and c3, a queen's bishop on b2 would look at its own pawn, the very fianchetto the b3 pawn was meant for. Three queenside pawn moves and none that contests the centre leave White well behind.

1.b3 e5 2.a3 d5 3.c3 Nf6.strategy: Develops with a purpose: the knight eyes e4 and supports d5, so a central push by White would be hard to carry out. Black needs nothing special; development and castling are enough against a set-up that does not challenge the centre.
